findings.note: Context binding is checked before any snapshot in both _physics_process and _record_sample, and _write_invalid is guarded by `finished`, so an invalidated scene emits valid=false with an explicit reason and empty final exactly once. The order app -> run_mode -> body count -> per-body identity -> episode -> revision matches the reasons the test expects for teardown/mode_off (physics_removed), app_free (app_removed), rebuild (body_removed|body_context_changed) and new_episode (episode_changed). Supplied runtime evidence shows each invalid case written at the same physics tick (36) as the context action, with no engine errors, which is consistent with the code.

The evaluator never calls into agent_loop/run_mode mutators; it only reads state and connects to frame_ready/body_entered. new_episode evidence shows the replacement owner enabled and producing frame 2 after the observer invalidated, satisfying the no-cancellation requirement.

_snapshot hard-codes run_mode.bodies[0], [3], [4] but _ready only rejects when wall is missing or robot is empty. A graph with fewer than five bodies that still contains a stage_wall would raise an index error instead of unsupported_fixture. Not reachable with the fixed RobotCarPreset fixture used here; worth a size guard if the observer is reused.

The early physics_unavailable path writes before _episode_id/_revision are captured, so that result carries an empty episode_id. Harmless for the tested modes, but the record is less self-describing than the other invalid reasons.

app.app_controller is dereferenced without an is_instance_valid check, unlike run_mode and agent_loop. Safe while app_controller is owned by main.tscn and freed with app, but inconsistent with the rest of the guard.

Rebuild accepts either body_removed or body_context_changed because the outcome depends on whether old bodies are freed or queue_freed within the same tick; this is documented in the reasons table and acceptable, but it means the test does not pin down one deterministic reason.

The test confirms a final result exists and its shape, but does not verify it was written only once (e.g. by checking that camera-calibration.jsonl stops growing or by stamping the result). Single emission currently rests on the `finished` guard in code review rather than on an assertion.

Registration expands the lifecycle script into seven independent rendered checks with `-- --lifecycle-mode <mode>` as the trailing arguments, excludes --headless and --ssok-agent-bridge, and skips the generic single-check registration. The Python test asserts exactly these properties and that the unsuffixed name is absent. The headless early exit returns 2, which the runner treats as failure, so a misconfigured headless run cannot pass silently.

Two frame_post_draw waits before agent_loop.begin() keep shader setup out of the unchanged 60s operation watchdog without modifying app code. This is a test-harness mitigation, not a product fix, and should not be read as cold-start reliability.

Changes are limited to the observer, test, CI registration, generated map and evidence. No app src/UI/camera/controller/physics/goal/provider/default/package files are touched, and there is no user-facing text, so no localization update is required.

remaining_limits: This review is static reading of the supplied files, diff and runtime summary; the reviewer did not rerun any command or inspect screenshots.
Each mode has a single supplied passing run; flakiness across repeated runs is not characterized.
Cold-cache startup reliability is not established: an earlier cold-cache rebuild process timed out, and the tracked test relies on a warm Mesa cache plus two warm-up draws.
The original AI case 9 context-change initiator remains unidentified; this work only makes the observer fail closed when such a change occurs.
No mode exercises a context change or Stop while a drive action is pending (acting/settling state); all context actions occur from the ready state.
The unsupported_collision_shape and unsupported_fixture paths are not exercised by the tracked test.
Results pertain to observer correctness only; they do not demonstrate optical goal adoption or success of the original physical goal.
Native rendered checks are owned by the coordinator; integration rebase and merge remain with the integration owner and the human respectively.
coordinator_clarifications: Actual operation watchdog10seconds; ready decision watchdog60seconds. Reviewer60second operation wording is a static factual error, not the basis for runtime acceptance.
